blocking.section: Binary upgrades > In-place handover (step 5, Steer); Binary upgrades intro
blocking.issue: Previous items L1-1 to L1-9 are resolved. This is a new finding in the revised steering step. After the CBPF swap, the old process accepts its queue and then closes its listeners. On Linux, that close still resets two kinds of connection. First, handshakes that were in SYN_RECV on the old listener before the swap: when the final ACK arrives after the close, the request is dropped, the lookup finds the new listener, and the new listener answers the unmatched ACK with an RST (no SYN cookie was issued). Second, children that complete their handshake between the old process's last accept() returning EAGAIN and close(): inet_csk_listen_stop resets them. Go cannot drain an accept queue and close it atomically. The window is about the connection rate times the client RTT, so at half saturation with 100 ms clients it is tens of resets per handover (hypothesis). This is the failure HAProxy measured. So 'CBPF steering, emptying the closing accept queue, closes that gap' is not true as written. ZG-3 and the V-3 pass criterion ('Zero refused or reset connections' over 1,000 handovers) cannot be met. Only net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req=1 (Linux 5.14+) moves in-progress requests and late children to the remaining socket on close. The document calls it 'the alternative' to the CBPF swap, but for this window it is the complement.
blocking.evidence: Step 5: "Once accepted, the new process listens; the holder swaps each program to select it through `golang.org/x/sys/unix` (`net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req` is the alternative), accepts its queue and closes its listeners, losing QUIC connections here, not at bind."; line 138: "CBPF steering, emptying the closing accept queue, closes that gap."; ZG-3: "An in-place handover refuses no new TCP connection"; V-3 pass: "Zero refused or reset connections and failed requests"
blocking.fix: In step 5, after the swap the holder keeps accepting for a linger of at least 3 s (target), which covers handshakes started before the swap, including one SYN-ACK retransmission. Only then does it close. Also state that handover hosts SHOULD set net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req=1 (Linux 5.14 or later, per network namespace). With it, closing migrates both queued children and in-progress handshakes to the new socket, even with a CBPF program attached (selection falls back to hash over the remaining sockets). Reword line 138 to match. Qualify ZG-3 as 'with tcp_migrate_req=1; without it, only handshakes needing more than one SYN-ACK retransmission across the linger can be reset (hypothesis)'. Run V-3 in both modes, recording resets per handover. Record the pack change under foundation amendments rather than contradicting pack section 7 in the text.

blocking.section: Verification runbook (During any upgrade row) vs Control plane upgrades and Kubernetes Drain and restart
blocking.issue: The runbook applies a pass criterion to every upgrade: `ruralz_control_cluster_nodes` drops at most 10%. The document's own procedures predictably break it. Replacing one of three Ruralz Control replicas unqualifies that replica's Nodes, about a third of the Cluster, for 10 minutes. The document says so, and V-5 depends on OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-14 (a). A T4 rolling update with declared ceilings needs no pacing, and it removes M = 100 of 1,000 Nodes every 45 s. Each drained Node drops out of the count at once and rejoins only 10 minutes later, so within 7.5 minutes the published count falls far beyond 10%. An operator following the runbook would fail, or halt, every Ruralz Control upgrade and every unpaced T4 update.
blocking.evidence: Runbook: "During any upgrade | `ruralz_control_cluster_nodes`; `ruralz_node_degraded_info{reason=\"state_store_breaker_open\"}` | Drops at most 10% (target); no breaker opens"; Control plane upgrades: "Until OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-14 closes, each replacement unqualifies its Nodes"; Node count during upgrades: "a `draining` Heartbeat drops a Node at once, and it rejoins only 10 minutes plus a 10%-per-minute ramp later (target)" and "declared ceilings ... need no pacing"; Kubernetes: "Example N = 1,000, minReplicas 300, three zones: M = 100, 10 steps, 7.5 min (hypothesis)"
blocking.fix: Scope the row. For derived-ceiling Clusters upgraded under the 10%-per-10-minutes pacing, the count drops at most 10% (target) and no breaker opens. For declared-ceiling Clusters, only 'no breaker opens' applies, and the count drop is expected. For Ruralz Control upgrades, until OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-14 (a), expect a drop of up to the replaced replica's share of Nodes, and check that derived-ceiling Clusters declared per-Node ceilings before starting. Keep V-5's dependency note consistent with this.

non_blocking.suggestion: The old process reports usage each second (target), so right after a burst of 1001 closes, the new process sees stale usage. Near the connection ceiling, it could refuse reconnects that the old process has already released. Have the old process send a usage update before each batch of going-away closes, or give the new process a small burst allowance equal to the closes announced in the last report.

Between acceptance and closing its Control Stream, the holder can still receive a Snapshot or Delta, activate it and ACK it. The new process then serves an older Revision until its Hello resyncs. State that once the holder has accepted, it defers or transiently NACKs new configuration until the Control Stream moves, so the Node never reports an ACKed digest it does not serve.

non_blocking.section: Binary upgrades > In-place handover; Plugin hot-swap
non_blocking.suggestion: With Plugin memory shared, the new process's pools may warm to 0 when the old process's pools hold most of maxPluginMemoryBytes, and the first requests then hit RZ-PLG under failureMode. That would fail V-3's zero-failed-requests criterion. Have the old process shrink idle pool instances as soon as steering completes, and add Plugin-bearing Routes to V-3.
